name: Sludge incineration and co-incineration
applications: urban plants with no land for biosolids
principle: Published practice: dewatered sludge is fired in fluidised-bed or multiple-hearth furnaces (self-sustaining above ~28% DS with heat recovery to steam/hot flue gas); flue gas cleaning (SNCR, fabric filters, wet scrubbers) meets EU IED; mono-ash retains phosphorus for recovery (e.g. EasyMining Ash2Product); co-incineration routes sludge to cement kilns or coal plants.

process_steps.name: Flue gas treatment
equipment: SNCR, fabric filter, wet scrubber stages

costs.basis: EPA 832-F-03-013: operating costs in one study range from USD 83 to USD 269 per dry Mg (USD 76-245 per dry ton), adjusted using 2002 ENR values. Comparable figures in the same sheet: landfill USD 127/dry Mg (USD 115/dry ton), land application about USD 15.40/dry Mg (USD 14/dry ton).

source.note: US EPA, Biosolids Technology Fact Sheet: Use of Incineration for Biosolids Management, EPA 832-F-03-013, COSTS section (costs adjusted using 2002 ENR values)

gaps.item: capital cost per tonne per day of installed incineration capacity
gaps.reason: Operating cost per dry Mg is now recorded (2002 basis, EPA 832-F-03-013). The sheet gives one facility capital quote (USD 6 million for a two-plant facility) without a capacity basis usable as a unit cost.
